info.title: Florensic API
info.description:
Backend for the Florensic houseplant app.

All errors use `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"?}}`; `message` is safe to show to users.
Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`; access tokens last 15 minutes, use
`POST /v1/auth/refresh` to rotate.

post.summary: Sign in with Apple or Google id-token

get.description:
Catalogue matches first, then iNaturalist for plants we don't carry yet.

Declared before `/{species_id}` so "suggest" is not read as a species UUID.

post.summary: Turn a picked suggestion into a species you can keep
post.description:
200 when we already had the plant, 201 when this call drafted it.

A first resolve of a plant nobody has picked before takes about ten seconds: one text
model call writes its care card. Every later resolve of the same plant, under any of
its names, is a lookup.

201.description: The species was drafted for the catalogue.

post.summary: Check in on a plant with a photo
post.description:
Spec §6.3: the check-in job was created (and its analysis quota counted) by the
`purpose=checkin` upload and left `queued`; this is where the owner's own report joins
it and the job finally runs. Poll `GET /v1/analysis/{job_id}` for the result.

400.description: `photo_wrong_purpose` — the photo wasn't uploaded for a check-in

409.description: `photo_already_used` — that photo's check-in has already run

429.description: `analysis_quota_exceeded` — counted once, by the upload that created the job

post.summary: Log a quick note about a plant
post.description:
The owner's own report, with no photo and no model call.

Chips, not free text alone: a phrase a model has to read costs a call and answers
slowly, while a tapped chip maps straight onto the taxonomy
(`app/modules/care/chips.yaml`) and can pull the next check-in forward the moment it
is tapped. The optional `text` rides along for the reviewer and for the timeline; it
is never parsed.

What it writes is a `note` **finding** per mapped chip — a claim about the plant
carrying no severity and no confidence, invisible to every score until the next
check-in's reviewer confirms it from a photograph.

409.description: `plant_not_active` — a paused plant takes no notes

post.summary: Skip a watering, with a reason
post.description:
"Not this time, and here is why."

Beside `water` rather than inside it, because it is the opposite answer to the same
question and the care score has to tell them apart: a watering skipped because the soil
was still wet is care given, and one skipped because the owner was away is not.

409.description: `plant_not_active` — a paused plant has no watering due

schema.title: Response Today V1 Care Today Get

404.description: `task_not_found` — not on this owner's list today

post.description:
Answer a treatment step with "not this time".

The step is recorded as `skipped` with the reason and does **not** come back on its
cadence — the chain ends there. It still counts as care that was due and not given,
so the care score reflects it; a step the owner could not do is a fact about the
plant's care, not a step that was never asked for.

404.description: `task_not_found` — not on this owner's list today

post.summary: Upload a plant photo and start analysis

get.summary: Poll an identification or check-in job
Daily insights and the humidity correlation
get.description:
Today and the 29 days before it of the caller's insights — 30 days exactly,
newest first.

`correlation` is computed live rather than stored: it moves every time a health
point or a snapshot lands, and it is two cheap grouped reads, so caching it would
only buy a way for it to go stale. It is null for a user with no home cell — there
is no weather series to compare their plants against.

Nothing here carries a cell or a coordinate. The feed is about the owner's plants,
and where they live is the one thing the client already knows.

Today's home screen: the owner's local climate, the species they might like next,
what their plants have done lately, and what is in flower around them.

Cached per user for an hour, so opening the app repeatedly costs one computation.
Nothing in the response says where the owner lives.

Every treatment this plant has had, newest first, with its steps in order.

The history, not a to-do list: closed treatments stay, because what was prescribed
for a problem last time is exactly what the owner wants to see when it comes back.
Today's outstanding steps are on `GET /v1/care/today` as `treatment_step` tasks.

schema.title: Response List Treatments V1 Plants  Plant Id  Treatments Get

get.description:
Every treatment plan this plant has had, newest first.

The owner-facing shape of `GET /v1/plants/{id}/treatments`: the same rows, grouped
into the plans they were prescribed as. One scan that found three problems is **one**
course with three `problems` and one ordered list of `steps` — shared steps first
(labelled `serves: "all"`), then the members worst first — rather than three courses
the owner has to reconcile.

The history, not a to-do list: closed courses stay, because what was prescribed last
time is exactly what the owner wants to see when a problem comes back. Today's
outstanding steps are on `GET /v1/care/today` as `treatment_step` tasks, in this same
order.

schema.title: Response List Courses V1 Plants  Plant Id  Courses Get

post.description:
"I am not doing this", or "it is better now".

The one way a treatment closes that is not the check-in reviewer's doing, and the
`reason` is what the system acts on: `plant_recovered` closes it as a resolution,
`too_hard` as care refused and buys the problem a fortnight's cooldown before the same
course can be prescribed again, `other` as neither. Either way the remaining steps stop
appearing on today's list and the check-in cadence the treatment shortened goes back.

Returns the treatment as it now is, so the client can redraw the row it was looking at
without re-fetching the plant's whole history.

"I am not doing any of this", or "it is all better now".

`POST /v1/treatments/{id}/abandon` for every open problem on the plan, in one
transaction and with one reason — and the per-treatment route stays, for an owner who
has finished with one problem and not the others. What the `reason` means is unchanged:
`plant_recovered` resolves each member and each member's finding, `too_hard` counts as
care refused and buys every one of those problems a fortnight's cooldown, `other` is
neither. The check-in cadence the plan shortened goes back when the last member closes.

Returns the course as it now is, so the client can redraw the plan it was looking at.

409.description: `course_not_open` — every problem on it has finished

get.description:
What `care.problem_metrics` (04:00 UTC) made of each problem over the trailing 90
days: how often the owner and the model disagreed, how often an owner's quick note was
confirmed, how often a course resolved inside the horizon the taxonomy promised, how
long it took, and how often the owner gave up.

Every rate is `null` when its own denominator was zero. A dashboard that rendered those
as `0%` would be reporting a failure where there was simply nothing to measure.

403.description: `admin_only` — signed in, but not an admin

BloomOut.title: BloomOut
BloomOut.description:
One species people near the owner have photographed in flower this month
(home-feed-design, "Blooming nearby").

`species_id` is set when the plant is one we carry, so the card's row taps straight
through to our own species page; it is null for the rest, which are still worth
showing. The row carries no coordinates: "near you" is as precise as it gets.

CarePlanItemOut.title: CarePlanItemOut
CarePlanItemOut.description: Mirrors `CarePlanItem` minus `plan_id`, which is redundant on a per-plan response.

ChangeOut.title: ChangeOut
ChangeOut.description:
One thing one of the owner's plants has done lately, as the changes card shows it
(home-feed-design, "Changes"): `since` is when this run of check-ins started, `count`
how many of them said it, and `detail` the sentence the app prints.

CheckinResultOut.title: CheckinResultOut
CheckinResultOut.description: Spec §6.3 step 7: everything a finished check-in changed, in one block.

ClimateOut.title: ClimateOut
ClimateOut.description:
What the owner's weather has been like lately, in one line of copy and four
numbers. It carries no cell and no coordinates: the card says "tropical and humid",
never where that was measured.

ConditionUpdateIn.title: ConditionUpdateIn
ConditionUpdateIn.description: The owner's own report on a check-in, posted once the photo is uploaded.

CorrelationOut.title: CorrelationOut
CorrelationOut.description:
The humid-vs-dry correlation card, built from `rules.correlation()`'s dict. The
five fields are fixed and always present together — never a bare object.

CourseOut.title: CourseOut
CourseOut.description:
One plant's plan for every problem it is being treated for.

Derived, not stored: a course is a `course_id` shared by its member rows, and every
field here is a fact about those rows (`course.course_view`). It is open while any
member is, as grave as its worst member, started when its first member did and
reviewed when its earliest open member is.

`steps` is the whole plan in one order — shared steps first, then the members worst
first, then the protocol's own position — because that is the order the owner is meant
to work through it, and it is the same order `GET /v1/care/today` uses.

CourseProblemOut.title: CourseProblemOut
CourseProblemOut.description:
One problem on a course — the member row, without its steps.

The steps are on `CourseOut` instead, as one list in the order the owner should work
through them, because a course is one plan and splitting it per problem is exactly the
reading audit gap 2 was about. Everything here is about *this problem*: how it is
going, when it is judged, and how it ended if it has.

CourseStepOut.title: CourseStepOut
CourseStepOut.description:
One step of a course, with the problem it is for already resolved.

`TreatmentStepOut` says which **row** a step hangs from (`treatment_id`) and whether it
is shared (`serves`); working out which *problem* it is for from those two means
joining back to `problems[]`. `GET /v1/care/today` already answers that question
directly for a `treatment_step` task, and two surfaces answering the same question two
ways is a thing a client gets wrong once each.

DailyInsightOut.title: DailyInsightOut
DailyInsightOut.description:
One card in the feed. Deliberately carries no cell, no coordinates and no owner:
`data` holds only the numbers the copy quotes (spec §9).

FindingOut.title: FindingOut
FindingOut.description:
One typed problem the analysis saw, as the app reads it back. `problem_id` is the
taxonomy id (`app/modules/care/problems.yaml`) the free-text `name` was filed under,
and is null only for rows written before the taxonomy existed.

HomeMetaOut.title: HomeMetaOut
HomeMetaOut.description:
`generated_at` is the instant the feed was computed, not the instant it was
served — a cached feed carries the older one, which is exactly what tells the app
how fresh the cards are.

`timezone` is the **owner's** zone since Phase 6, because the dates in this document
are their days now. It was `"UTC"`, which was true while every date here was UTC's and
became a correct-sounding lie the moment they stopped being. A cached feed carries the
zone it was built with, like `generated_at`.

HomeOut.title: HomeOut
HomeOut.description:
The whole home screen in one document. Every card is independent: a missing input
— no home cell, no plants, a provider down — is `null` or `[]` for that card and
never an error for the rest.

InsightsMetaOut.title: InsightsMetaOut
InsightsMetaOut.description:
`timezone` is the **owner's** zone since Phase 6: `Insight.day` is written on their
calendar and the feed is scoped by it, so a `"UTC"` here would be describing a
document whose dates are no longer UTC's.

InsightsOut.title: InsightsOut
InsightsOut.description:
`correlation` is built from `rules.correlation()`'s dict, or null when there is
not enough history — or no home cell to read the weather of.

NextPlantOut.title: NextPlantOut
NextPlantOut.description:
One catalogue species the owner does not keep yet, with the one-line reason it
was picked (home-feed-design, "Suggestions").

NoteIn.title: NoteIn
NoteIn.description:
A quick note: what the owner tapped, and optionally what they typed.

At least one chip and no repeats. An empty note is nothing to record, and the same
chip twice is the same report twice — both are a client bug, and a 422 says so rather
than writing a timeline entry nobody meant.

`text` is never parsed. It reaches the check-in reviewer and the timeline as the
owner's own words; everything the system acts on comes from the chips.

PlanMetaOut.title: PlanMetaOut
PlanMetaOut.description:
`timezone` is the owner's, like the home and insights feeds' (Phase 7a).

It said `"UTC"` through Phase 6, and that was a statement of fact rather than an
oversight: a plan item's `due_at` and a treatment step's dates were written from
`revise_plan`'s UTC `now`, so UTC really was the calendar this document's own dates
were on. They are now dated from `local_today(owner)` — threaded into `revise_plan`,
`open_treatment` and the review drafts — so the field follows, as that docstring said
it would.

The default is still `"UTC"`, for a caller that builds the document with no user in
hand; `GET /v1/plants/{id}/care-plan` passes the owner's zone.

PlantSpeciesIn.title: PlantSpeciesIn
PlantSpeciesIn.description: The species the owner says this plant really is.

ProblemMetricsPage.title: ProblemMetricsPage
ProblemMetricsPage.description:
`window_end` is the newest window any of these rows is from.

With a `window_end` asked for it is that date and every row shares it. Without one, each
problem contributes its **own latest window** — a problem nothing has happened to for a
week has no row for last night, and leaving it out would read as "this problem went away"
rather than "nothing happened" — so the rows can be from different dates and this field
is the newest of them. Each row carries its own `window_end`, which is what to read.

ResolveIn.title: ResolveIn
ResolveIn.description: A suggestion the user picked, sent back as it was received.

RiskOut.title: RiskOut
RiskOut.description:
What is about to go wrong, and why, in the owner's own words.

Computed on every read and never stored (`app/modules/health/risk.py`): a risk is a
claim about the coming week, and one computed last night would be a claim about a
week that has already started. `reasons` is empty exactly when `level` is `low`.

`breakdown` carries every rule with its outcome, including the ones that did not
fire, plus what the inputs were (`weather: "unavailable"` versus a calm week,
`ever_observed`, `active_treatments`). It is published for the same reason the health
score's own breakdown is: a number nobody can take apart is a number nobody can argue
with. It is not a display shape — `level` and `reasons` are — and it may change
without notice.

SuggestionOut.title: SuggestionOut
SuggestionOut.description:
One typeahead row, always a species. `species_id` is set for plants we already
carry; an `inaturalist` row names a plant we would draft on `POST /species/resolve`.

TaskSkipIn.title: TaskSkipIn
TaskSkipIn.description:
The owner's reason for skipping a treatment step. Optional: a skip with no reason
is still better information than a step left pending for a fortnight.

TreatmentAbandonIn.title: TreatmentAbandonIn
TreatmentAbandonIn.description:
Why the owner is stopping a course.

A closed list, because the three answers mean three different things and the service
acts on the difference: `plant_recovered` is a resolution (the remaining steps stop
counting against the owner, the finding is resolved, the problem returning is a
recurrence), `too_hard` is care refused and buys the problem a cooldown, and `other` is
neither. Free text could not be told apart, and guessing would be the system deciding
what the owner meant.

`note` is the owner's own words, for the timeline. It is never parsed.

WaterSkipIn.title: WaterSkipIn
WaterSkipIn.description:
Why this watering is not happening.

A closed list, not free text, because the three answers mean three different things to
the care score and the schedule: `soil_wet` is care given (and pushes the next watering
out), while `away` and `forgot` are care not given and change nothing but the record.
